metadata.title: Equilateral simplices over general fields
metadata.abstract: A classical theorem of Schoenberg (1937) characterizes the dimensions $d$ for which $\mathbb{Q}^d$ contains the vertex set of a regular simplex with $d+1$ vertices. We generalize Schoenberg's result to all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$, using elementary Witt theory and Lagrange's four-square theorem. Our generalization also sharpens Schoenberg's theorem and complements more recent work of Lorenz and Zimmermann (2026) by characterizing the admissible edge lengths. In the case of finite characteristic, equilateral simplices with $d+2$ vertices can sometimes exist (F.~Radó 1986), and we characterize this situation as well, again for all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$. We also briefly consider the edge lengths of equilateral simplices of $d$ vertices.
